summary: Network Mobility for Mobile IPv4 (NEMOv4) lets a whole moving network, such as one in a vehicle, stay connected. This RFC defines a dynamic prefix allocation mechanism for it.

eli5.summary: If a whole bus full of laptops moves around, it needs a block of addresses to give them. This explains how the bus gets and changes that block.

questions: what is dynamic prefix allocation for network mobility
how does a mobile router request a prefix
subtitle: How a Mobile Router asks its home agent to hand out network prefixes instead of configuring them by hand.

tldr.problem: The base NEMOv4 specification lets a Mobile Router register mobile network prefixes, but it does not let the home agent allocate them dynamically.
tldr.mechanism: The Mobile Router sets the Prefix field of a Mobile Network Request extension to zero, and the home agent may answer with a Mobile Network Acknowledgement carrying the prefix it chose.
tldr.outcome: It adds one new code, 4 (MOBNET_UNASSIGNED), to the Mobile Network Acknowledgement registry and updates RFC 5177.

facts.label: Prefix lifetime
facts.value: Same as the binding cache entry

today: RFC 6626 is a Proposed Standard from May 2012 that updates RFC 5177. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The base NEMOv4 specification, RFC 5177, defines extensions to Mobile IPv4 for mobile networks. This document adds support for dynamic allocation of mobile prefixes by the home agent.

It is a Standards Track document and updates RFC 5177.
sections.eli5: A moving network used to have to bring its own addresses. Now it can ask its home base to assign them.

sections.title: The Mobile Router Side
sections.content:
To ask for a prefix, the Mobile Router MUST set the Prefix field of the Mobile Network Request extension to zero. It MAY set the prefix length field to zero, or to a length of its choice as a hint to the home agent. Such extensions MAY appear in the initial registration or a later one.

On a registration reply, the router processes it as Mobile IPv4 and RFC 5177 require. If network acknowledgement extensions carry the Code Success, the router SHOULD treat the listed prefixes as allocated and create the bindings defined in RFC 5177. If it gets Code 1, "invalid prefix", it may take that as a hint that the home agent does not support dynamic allocation.
sections.eli5: The router says 'give me some addresses, any will do' by leaving the address blank. It may suggest a size, and then uses whatever it is given.

sections.title: The Home Agent Side
sections.content:
A home agent that receives a request with a zero Prefix MAY reply with a Mobile Network Acknowledgement whose Prefix field holds the allocated prefix. The length is the home agent's choice, though it MAY consider the hint. Once it allocates a prefix, it MUST maintain the prefix registration table from RFC 5177. The prefix lifetime equals the lifetime of the binding cache entry.

The home agent may instead return one of the negative codes from RFC 5177. A router may ask for several prefixes, and for any that could not be assigned the Code should be set to 4 (MOBNET_UNASSIGNED).

This can be combined with dynamic home address allocation: the home address field may be zero while the request also carries zero-Prefix extensions. If the home address is not zero it MAY identify the client; otherwise the NAI extension needs to be included and SHOULD be used to identify the Mobile Router.
sections.eli5: The home office picks the addresses, decides how many fit, and keeps a list of who got what. If it has none to give, it says so with a special code.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The specification works within the security constraints of Mobile IPv4, the NAI extension and RFC 5177. Home agents SHOULD take steps to prevent address exhaustion attacks, for example by limiting the number and size of prefixes any one Mobile Router can be allocated.

IANA assigned value 4, MOBNET_UNASSIGNED (Home Agent cannot assign a mobile network prefix), in the Mobile Network Acknowledgement Extension registry.
sections.eli5: A greedy router could ask for every address. So the home office should put a limit on how much each one may take.

messages.label: Registration Request
messages.note: Mobile Network Request extension with Prefix set to zero.

messages.label: Registration Reply
messages.note: Network acknowledgement with the allocated prefix, or a negative code.
